title: Impact of Grade Retention on Future Academic Performance

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)

Why: Retention is assigned mechanically by whether the end-of-year test score falls below a known cutoff. Students just above and just below the cutoff are assumed to be quasi-randomly different, making local comparisons credible.

Key assumptions  
1. Continuity: In the absence of retention, the conditional expectation of future test scores is a smooth function of the running variable at the cutoff.  
2. No manipulation: Students (or teachers) cannot precisely manipulate scores around the cutoff.  
3. Sharp design: Treated = 1 if and only if the running variable is below the cutoff (verified in the data).

## 2. R Code
```r
#############################################
# Impact of Grade Retention on Future Scores
#############################################

# 1. Packages ------------------------------------------------------------
need <- c("data.table", "rdrobust", "rddensity")
new  <- need[!(need %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new)) install.packages(new, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
lapply(need, require, character.only = TRUE)

# 2. Load data -----------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s97_data.csv"
dat  <- fread(path)

# 3. Quick checks --------------------------------------------------------
# Cutoff assumed at 0
cutoff <- 0
# Verify sharp design
table_below <- with(dat, table(below_cutoff = running_var < cutoff, treated))
print(table_below)

# 4. Main RDD estimate (local linear, MSE-optimal BW) --------------------
rdr <- rdrobust(y = dat$y, x = dat$running_var, c = cutoff)
print(rdr)

# Extract point estimate
tau  <- rdr$coef[1]        # treatment effect at cutoff
se   <- rdr$se[1]
cat("\nMain RDD estimate (local linear, MSE-optimal BW):\n",
    "Effect of retention on future score =",
    round(tau, 4), " (SE =", round(se, 4), ")\n")

# 5. Robustness checks ---------------------------------------------------

## 5a. Different bandwidth (±0.20)
rdr_narrow <- rdrobust(y = dat$y, x = dat$running_var, c = cutoff, h = 0.20)
cat("\nRDD with ±0.20 bandwidth:\n",
    "Estimate =", round(rdr_narrow$coef[1], 4),
    " (SE =", round(rdr_narrow$se[1], 4), ")\n")

## 5b. Different polynomial order (quadratic)
rdr_quad <- rdrobust(y = dat$y, x = dat$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 2)
cat("\nRDD with quadratic control (p = 2):\n",
    "Estimate =", round(rdr_quad$coef[1], 4),
    " (SE =", round(rdr_quad$se[1], 4), ")\n")

## 5c. Placebo cutoff at +0.30
placebo_cut <- 0.30
rdr_placebo <- rdrobust(y = dat$y, x = dat$running_var, c = placebo_cut)
cat("\nPlacebo cutoff at +0.30:\n",
    "Estimate =", round(rdr_placebo$coef[1], 4),
    " (SE =", round(rdr_placebo$se[1], 4), ")\n")

## 5d. McCrary density test
dens <- rddensity(x = dat$running_var, c = cutoff)
print(dens)
cat("\nMcCrary density test p-value =", round(dens$test$p_jk[1], 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic intuition and prior literature suggest that forcing a child to repeat a grade tends to hamper subsequent performance (stigma, disengagement, age-for-grade mismatch). Therefore:

• Sign: Negative (retained students score lower in the future).  
• Magnitude: Roughly ‑0.10 to ‑0.20 standard deviations, so an RDD coefficient around −0.12 to −0.18 in the test-score units supplied.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The analysis exploits the cutoff in test scores to identify the causal effect.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Students retained due to scoring below the cutoff perform worse on future tests.
